title: Machine learning predicts chronic kidney disease progression after radical nephrectomy
summary: Five machine learning models were developed on 649 patients from eight centres to predict chronic kidney disease progression after radical nephrectomy for renal carcinoma. The best model, LightGBM, reached an AUC of 0.7508 internally and 0.7549 in a 320-patient external cohort from seven other centres. The study is retrospective and the AUC is modest.
ai_technology: LightGBM (best of five machine learning models) with SHAP
organization: Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital; Juntendo University

evidence.tested: AUC in an internal validation set and an external cohort of 320 patients from seven centres.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; modest AUC; clinical benefit not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient boosting models predicting CKD progression within three years.
